clean_body: There are plenty of reasons why we need to do whatever it takes to defend our narrow Senate majority, but I’ll do my best to narrow down the list to 5. | = Folks, There are plenty of reasons why we need to do whatever it takes to defend our narrow Senate majority, but I’ll do my best to narrow down the list to 5. = | = | = Alright, here we go! 1. Abortion rights: Republican legislators are rolling back abortion rights around the country. One of Senate Republicans’ top priorities is to pass a national abortion ban. 2. Climate crisis: We can’t take chances when it comes to preserving our planet. Democrats passed the largest investment in green energy and jobs in our country’s history, and Republicans are eager to repeal it. 3. Voting rights: When more people vote, Democrats win. So the GOP wants to make it harder for people to vote by chipping away at the Voting Rights Act and passing voting restrictions. 4. Lowering costs: A Republican-controlled Senate would pass another massive tax cut for corporations and the ultra-wealthy, leaving working families to shoulder the burden. 5. The Supreme Court: We’ve already seen the far-right court overturn Roe and overrule student debt relief. Democrats need Senate control to have a say in future nominations. For all these reasons (and so many more), we MUST defend our majority. But if we lose in Maryland, Republicans have a clear path to taking the Senate. = | | = | = | = | | = | = | = | = Thanks, Angela Alsobrooks * | | = Paid for by Elfreth for Maryland Elfreth for Maryland PO Box 5935 Annapolis, MD 21403 United States

Peter,

My opponent, Democrat Jon Tester, is trying to convince voters that he hasn't lost his way during his 18 years in Washington. During our first debate earlier this month, his desperation was palpable.

Do you recall when, during his 2012 re-election campaign, Barack Obama stood in front of a crowd and claimed that private industry wouldn't exist without the help of the federal government? It was one of the many instances I wondered if the president of the United States didn't believe in market-based capitalism that fueled America's rise to the top.

I'm a former Navy SEAL and a patriotic American. The small business I started a decade ago in Belgrade, Montana, has brought **[millions of dollars to the state's economy while creating hundreds of good-paying jobs.](http://links.itsourgreatamerica.com/u/click?_t=442fb7cf105f4725a8bda0b6bcffc1bd&_m=2e545d2af6cb45aca00c1fe0a198cbcd&_e=WtW7kc0SShpBcVStWKVkfGm6p290LKW6s7n-CGTs7EOOu9Xass60nPEAYTvnV__dwX3BiRw4ADSAA2LRVJUPeyBph4NpKVGp5aoVnT3xsDE46O3j2Kv5QcxXfN-qE2xz8Wa6MX21v9OVF_AsaxmUzOt-mlfQLK_k4kj-H-YrXZl2gQFARt6ht8D--dGoCu-VFUKRLHCta7YC5MZlIfBkREpwqlPmU1I5pL5LEAo-p_81R8LlOf6OZEa5SdXG4XlIiRTuYEyzz8xivjTq2EHEQAfDqGjq56oSUrDaeGwhv2owrBVnrj80CkG_W2tWQfmRdhystg9HPb0DUOatHltty8B7c0o0LUntVw80ipWyOvj-efZiuGnMjfA5EJKh4odCGkguluzp4BOMK2Ejlrrucw%3D%3D) **

Dear Peter,
November 5 will be here before we know it. With that in mind, I want to share an important message.
With political tensions rising and the campaign rancor getting more personal, more vicious and uglier, I am focused on what the American people care about – peace, freedom and prosperity.
The major parties keep ratcheting up the political tension, but they do not address the needs, desires and solutions that make everyday Americans’ lives better. Instead of uniting, they divide.
I will not contribute to that kind of dirty politics. While the other campaigns fight for party power, I will fight for power to be returned to you, the people.
Running as an independent, I am able to focus on the issues and solutions that make your life better, not pay them lip service.
I intend to unite the country by focusing on innovative solutions that transcend party lines, like:
* Restoring the middle class with good jobs and affordable home ownership;
* Revitalizing small businesses;
* Ending the chronic disease epidemic affecting half our children;
* Securing our borders – especially from the drug cartels;
* Protecting our rivers and shorelines; and
* Freeing federal agencies from corporate control.

These are not partisan issues; they are American issues—issues that require us to come together for the common good.

body:
Peter, the heat index across Texas is reaching triple digits this week.
This kind of heat is extremely dangerous, especially for workers across our state who lack basic protections like water breaks, thanks to horrible legislation signed by Greg Abbott last year.
**That’s why nearly one year ago, I held a thirst strike in the hot sun on the steps of the U.S. Capitol for nearly nine hours—to draw attention to the need for a federal workplace heat standard.**
And now it’s in the news: the Biden administration will soon publish a proposed new heat safety standard for workers. That’s why it’s so important we continue this push now.
[**Can you chip in $8, $10, or whatever you can, to help Team Casar keep pushing for a federal heat safety standard? We’re so close to delivering these important protections for workers. Peter, there is no excuse for big corporations to deny employees working in deadly heat basic protections like water breaks. But unfortunately, that’s exactly what many are doing – and they have the full support of Greg Abbott.
In fact, last summer Greg Abbott signed a law eliminating the guarantee for water breaks for construction workers in Texas. It’s shameful.
I held a thirst strike to call attention to the lack of federal heat safety standards. And thanks to our push and the efforts of many others, they may soon be on the way. That means an estimated 50 million workers could be protected, even in states like Texas where their governor has abandoned them.
[**Peter******,** can you chip in $8 or $10 today to help us finally secure federal heat safety protections for American workers? clean_body: Peter, the heat index across Texas is reaching triple digits this week. This kind of heat is extremely dangerous, especially for workers across our state who lack basic protections like water breaks, thanks to horrible legislation signed by Greg Abbott last year. That’s why nearly one year ago, I held a thirst strike in the hot sun on the steps of the U.S. Capitol for nearly nine hours—to draw attention to the need for a federal workplace heat standard. And now it’s in the news: the Biden administration will soon publish a proposed new heat safety standard for workers. That’s why it’s so important we continue this push now. = ** Tom Williams/Getty Images = Peter, there is no excuse for big corporations to deny employees working in deadly heat basic protections like water breaks. But unfortunately, that’s exactly what many are doing – and they have the full support of Greg Abbott. In fact, last summer Greg Abbott signed a law eliminating the guarantee for water breaks for construction workers in Texas. It’s shameful. I held a thirst strike to call attention to the lack of federal heat safety standards. And thanks to our push and the efforts of many others, they may soon be on the way. That means an estimated 50 million workers could be protected, even in states like Texas where their governor has abandoned them. = Thank you, -Greg Greg Casar Congressman Texas Congressional District 35 ****=** | ****** ---|---

#
# **We Can Stop Gun Violence by Investing in Communities**
Senator Hughes recently brought together anti-violence community groups, gun violence advocates, and lawmakers to recognize **gun violence awareness month** and the impactful work of community violence intervention. The group gathered to call for more investments to support the work of local groups, made up of our friends and neighbors, who have been critical in stopping violence and promoting public safety. The rally was held following the release of data that showed a [16% decline in Philadelphia gun violence in 2024, compared to a national decline of 13%.](http://enews.senatorhughes.com/mail/util.cfm?mailaction=clickthru&gpiv=2100168109.172706.230&gen=1&mailing_linkid=10995) The data was shared in a [report from the Center for American Progress](http://enews.senatorhughes.com/mail/util.cfm?mailaction=clickthru&gpiv=2100168109.172706.230&gen=1&mailing_linkid=10996) that stated Philadelphia and other cities seeing gains in public safety have, "made significant investments in more holistic and long-term approaches to improving public safety...like supporting vulnerable community members, investing in community violence intervention models, and bolstering data tracking and gun violence reporting to better foster case resolution."
* * *
**" We can help neighborhood based organizations keep the momentum going of what they have already achieved and do even more. If we invest in communities, they will respond. We can't walk away from this responsibility."** **\- Senator Hughes -**
* * *
Senator Hughes and fellow speakers highlighted the need for more funding for Pennsylvania's [ Violence Intervention and Prevention (VIP) grant program](http://enews.senatorhughes.com/mail/util.cfm?mailaction=clickthru&gpiv=2100168109.172706.230&gen=1&mailing_linkid=10997), which invests money directly into community groups. In March, [Senator Hughes announced over $24 million dollars for community violence prevention groups and initiatives across Philadelphia and Montgomery Counties](http://enews.senatorhughes.com/mail/util.cfm?mailaction=clickthru&gpiv=2100168109.172706.230&gen=1&mailing_linkid=10998). Governor Shapiro has proposed $100 million for the VIP program for next year's budget. Lawmakers and advocates also discussed 3 commonsense gun laws- universal background checks, red flag laws, ghost gun regulations- that have passed in the House of Representatives and are waiting for a vote in the Senate. Governor Shapiro has said he will sign these bills into law if they make it to his desk A "yes" vote in the Senate would bring these bills to Governor Shapiro's desk!
* * *
**" The Senate needs to finish the job on three commonsense pieces of legislation. We thank the House of Representatives for taking their role in the majority seriously, and we ask Senate Republicans to stop blocking progress on these laws, that the majority of Pennsylvanians support."** **\- Senator Hughes -**
* * *

body:
Under Katie Porter’s Presidential Ethics Reform Act, presidents and vice presidents will be required to publicly disclose their tax returns.
# [](https://act.katieporter.com/go/9?t=1&akid=38929%2E3422442%2E1Mzh_r)
Derek, did you hear the good news?
[](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ttp-em-20240621?refcode=em20240621-38929&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&refcode2=38929_3422442_1Mzh_r&akid=38929%2E3422442%2E1Mzh_r)
That’s right — under Katie Porter’s Presidential Ethics Reform Act, presidents and vice presidents will be _required_ to **publicly disclose their tax returns.**
Derek, this is a big deal. Remember how Donald Trump refused to release his tax returns and financial records for _the entire time_ he served as President of the United States?
**Well, Katie Porter is doing something about that. But proposing this bill is just the first step — now we need to pass it.** **[For that to happen, we need to elect candidates who share Rep. Porter’s vision of restoring trust in government. Will you help us do that by chipping in $5 today?](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ttp-em-20240621?refcode=em20240621-38929&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&refcode2=38929_3422442_1Mzh_r&akid=38929%2E3422442%2E1Mzh_r)**
Not only did Trump refuse to disclose his finances, but remember that he was ordered to pay a **$355 _million_ fine** for committing fraud by lying about his wealth. Trump falsified business records and used fraudulent financial statements to obtain millions of dollars in loans.
It’s clear that “just trust me” isn’t good enough — candidates like Trump need to be required to disclose their tax returns and financial records. Voters have a right to know where their future leaders have been getting their money — and from whom.
**[Derek, let’s pass this law — your gift today will help Truth to Power elect candidates who will vote for this bill as soon as they get the chance. Will you pitch in $5 today?](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ttp-em-20240621?refcode=em20240621-38929&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&refcode2=38929_3422442_1Mzh_r&akid=38929%2E3422442%2E1Mzh_r)**

body:
These awesome leaders and activists have endorsed Sarah because they’ve seen her deliver results in the State Senate.
#
Friend, the whole team here at McBride HQ is _so proud_ of how much this campaign has grown since we launched last summer – and especially in the last week!
Within just the last few days, we’ve announced major endorsements from:
* Congresswoman **Lisa Blunt Rochester**
* U.S. Senator **Tom Carper**
* Delaware Governor **John Carney**
* Speaker Emerita **Nancy Pelosi**
* House Democratic Leader **Hakeem Jeffries**
* And a growing list of **state legislators and local officials**.

They join dozens of organizations – including Planned Parenthood, the AFL-CIO, End Citizens United – and hundreds of Delawareans up and down our state in support of Sarah.

_**Every 11 minutes, someone in the U.S. dies from gun violence.**_

It’s a chilling statistic, one that motivates me to continue pushing for life-saving gun violence prevention legislation, even as others oppose it.

I’ve dedicated my time in Congress to advocating for legislation that puts safety over the gun lobby. We must continue to invest in proven strategies like community-based violence intervention programs, mental health services, and commonsense gun safety measures.

[_**This Gun Violence Awareness Month, I recommit to ending senseless gun violence in our communities. Listen, every good hero needs a sidekick. Well, the same goes for candidates. Just take a look at our two options in NY-19 – the race that will decide control of the House in 2024\.

Josh Riley has me – dashingly handsome, incredibly smart, knock your socks off hilarious.

Republican Rep. Marc Molinaro has, well, look for yourself... [ ](https://act.fightforreform.org/go/45306?t=7&akid=21586%2E4449941%2EDVYYKs) [**My friend Josh Riley has to beat Molinaro and flip this must-win House seat. But with Trump wading in, Republican spending in NY-19 is about to skyrocket. Will you split a contribution between Josh and Fight for Reform to push back and help elect Democrats up and down the ballot?**](https://act.fightforreform.org/go/45306?t=8&akid=21586%2E4449941%2EDVYYKs) I don’t know about you, but if I was endorsed by someone who got convicted on 34 felony counts, I wouldn’t run around advertising it...

But I can’t say Molinaro’s endorsement surprises me. **Right after Trump’s conviction, MAGA Molinaro was right by his side, attacking our justice system and defending his criminal pal.**

Molinaro also stood by Trump’s when he threw out a woman’s right to choose, attacked Social Security, and incited a violent insurrection. So, what’s a few felonies between friends?

Look, these are the options. We can elect Josh Riley, who will always do what’s right for Upstate New York (and is friends with me to boot)! Or we can give Trump mini-me Marc Molinaro another two years in office and watch all our hard-fought progress go right down the toilet. I know which I’d prefer, and it’s not even close. [**So in the most competitive race in the country, it’s Al’s guy vs. Trump’s guy. If you’re with me on Team Josh Riley, will you split $7 between Josh and Fight for Reform to stand up to MAGA extremists and help elect state and local Democrats?**](https://act.fightforreform.org/go/45306?t=9&akid=21586%2E4449941%2EDVYYKs) If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your split donation between Fight for Reform and Josh Riley will go through immediately: | [CONTRIBUTE $7 »](https://act.fightforreform.org/go/45307?t=10&akid=21586%2E4449941%2EDVYYKs)

Al

Friend, my name is Hung Cao. I am a retired Navy Captain who served for 25 years in Special Operations. I served on the front lines defusing bombs for our SEAL teams and Special Forces; I also conducted some of the most dangerous deep dives in the military.
---
[](http://links.gopwinning.org/u/click?_t=ea36c899de41479ca8c7218c6a20a10b&_m=180f9c0918c64996897d464926ec76d9&_e=jlnyx8d_3Ek2AKWdr8TvmG9noZ4qh6_qh0C-xtaSD4An1wikzXm9RS2Sewz1770G1DD9K--R8Kkz4iqkZCEbKqpIMyaNx7bJ6oxS8OoeZsbJM4ujFbgdFJ7yMEZJI70uPqnYpruBLwmZZjCjooprs3ekzv5VJFXnvR9EUtOb7KsJO7neGG-e8nLyIcT7IOZIoVQ3irIlef76VKchhqPCLG2WF-LNeiTYqeMRmmWv_l892PQfplKyqeC1IT1jY5UZT6LePnnax7gKVVIUy4cfwGmWEtgX-1Hxt4a3Af8ZFT6S78cJiTjJIewMEGAlczStoAWY2DGaL8ofCNUEkmbwN5gshnWVQ2lcetKHvY4GgUz1ogbnOSaVGc6OtJJ2J7OTqPgemCbeGSHmpry2-C0Jog%3D%3D)
---
I was inspired to serve because America gave me everything. **My family escaped Communist Vietnam to the United States after the fall of Saigon. **
---
[](http://links.gopwinning.org/u/click?_t=ea36c899de41479ca8c7218c6a20a10b&_m=180f9c0918c64996897d464926ec76d9&_e=jlnyx8d_3Ek2AKWdr8TvmG9noZ4qh6_qh0C-xtaSD4An1wikzXm9RS2Sewz1770G1DD9K--R8Kkz4iqkZCEbKqpIMyaNx7bJ6oxS8OoeZsbJM4ujFbgdFJ7yMEZJI70uPqnYpruBLwmZZjCjooprs3ekzv5VJFXnvR9EUtOb7KsJO7neGG-e8nLyIcT7IOZIoVQ3irIlef76VKchhqPCLG2WF-LNeiTYqeMRmmWv_l_9aYgmVZei_r8mVJUL_YK7AHVynku4EHNh-jQuCfw_456a43n-0mLxqduxrGpnLACCz157_SeJS0ekgxCbzBERJsDoOL1PYMb-UgqpKgBPQAoLaJ9vam-cS_nZVVSZhMJ2GIGgwqclD0amvcWbq_zO4m9A8623sEDpGO4jIrr0Ig%3D%3D)
---
_If it wasn’t for America, I probably wouldn’t be alive today._

name: Heidi Ganahl
subject: The Mountain Minute: 6/21/2024
body:
Your daily rundown of REAL news for REAL Coloradans.
| | | | [](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
---
**PRESENTED BY[ROCKYMOUNTAINVOICE.COM](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
| | Hi friends,
This is the Mountain Minute for Friday, June 21, 2024.
- Heidi Ganahl
---
|
---
| | **TODAY'S TOP STORIES**
---
**[Rep. Soper: Gov. Polis dismissive of real concerns toward wolf depredation on Western Slope](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
A [weekend exchange](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) between a national columnist and Colorado Gov. Jared Polis has drawn the attention of Rep. Matt Soper, R-Delta, who pens commentary as "The Western Slope Statesman."
Soper took exception to the tone in which the governor responded to Helen Raleigh, a senior contributor at The Federalist and who had written a piece for the Wall Street Journal titled "[Jared Polis's Wolves Are Moving In on Denver](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)". Raleigh, an immigrant from China, is a Colorado resident.
"Colorado Gov. Jared Polis recently signed a bill to reintroduce the vicious weasel known as the wolverine to the state," Raleigh wrote on [Twitter/X](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.). "What could go wrong? Plenty, if Colorado's recent experience reintroducing the gray wolf is anything to go by."
**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---
**[Colorado ends budget year $164M in the red with potential tax cuts looming on November ballot](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** [THE COLORADO SUN](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* Colorado ends its fiscal year with a [$164 million deficit](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), compelling the state to utilize its reserves. Future budgets predict growing shortfalls, with potential mid-year adjustments needed due to factors like rising healthcare costs or decreased tax revenue.
* Concerns have escalated due to [two proposed conservative ballot measures](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) that could significantly reduce local property taxes and limit their growth, further complicating the budget scenario.
* If these measures pass, [drastic budget cuts](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) may be necessary, impacting education, healthcare, and local infrastructure.
* The state's financial analysts and the governor's office predict [severe repercussions](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), akin to those experienced during economic recessions, if the property tax initiatives are approved.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---
**[Flora heads up panel addressing'complex problem' of illegal immigration, HB 19-1124 and sanctuaries](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* In Douglas County, a forum featuring local law enforcement and political candidates addressed immigration issues, with a focus on securing the border and reversing sanctuary state policies implemented by [Colorado's House Bill 19-1124](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.).
* Participants, including Sheriff Darren Weekly and former ICE Director John Fabbricatore, [criticized the bill](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) for hindering cooperation with federal agencies and compromising public safety.
* The forum, organized by [U.S. House candidate Deborah Flora](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.). The panel discussed solutions including completing the border wall, defunding sanctuary cities, and enhancing federal law enforcement capabilities to address illegal immigration and drug trafficking.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---
**[Colorado ethics panel finds probable cause to investigate lawmaker accused of intoxication](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** [COLORADO POLITICS](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* A Colorado Senate panel has initiated an investigation into [Senator Faith Winter](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), following allegations she appeared intoxicated at a city council meeting. Accusations against Winter include exhibiting glassy eyes, slurred speech, and smelling of alcohol, leading to behavior described as disinterested, annoyed, and combative.
* Despite Winter's denial of being contacted about her conduct, multiple constituents and Northglenn City Council members voiced concerns, prompting an [ethics review](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.).
* The ethics committee is moving forward with probable cause to investigate further, focusing on whether [Winter's actions](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) at the meeting constituted an ethics violation.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---
**[New Colorado law protects tribal lands in response to contentious Durango, Southern Ute land dispute](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** [THE COLORADO SUN](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* Colorado enacted a law requiring cities to gain tribal approval for [annexing reservation lands](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), prompted by a dispute between Durango and the Southern Ute Indian Tribe.
* The law responds to concerns about Durango's [secretive expansion efforts](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) and ensures the protection of tribal sovereignty and lands. Tensions arose from Durango's development plans, which included potential annexation impacting tribal territories.
* The legislation complicates Durango's access to Lake Nighthorse [water resources](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), requiring tribal consent for any development plans involving annexation.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---
**[RFK Jr. misses CNN debate deadline, leaving Biden and Trump in head-to-head contest](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** [NATIONAL REVIEW](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* Robert F. Kennedy Jr. failed to meet [CNN's debate qualifications](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), missing the chance to join Joe Biden and Donald Trump on stage. He did not achieve the necessary 15% in four national polls or secure enough state ballot positions to represent 270 electoral votes.
* Kennedy [criticized his exclusion](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) as undemocratic and accused both major party candidates of colluding with CNN to keep him out. His campaign's efforts to gain ballot access continue, but his absence from the debate benefits Biden and Trump by reducing competition.
* This marks a [significant setback](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) for Kennedy as he seeks to challenge the two-party system in the upcoming presidential election.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|

name: Elizabeth Warren
subject: Add your name if you agree: Tax filing should be fast and free, and we can’t let Republicans stop us from making it happen
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Warren for Senate
body:
They’re trying to undo the progress we’ve fought so hard for.

| | | [ ](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/216?t=3&akid=2231%2E4032634%2E-NSXZV)
---
Congressional Republicans have a nasty habit that they just can’t seem to break: trying to keep costs high for working people. They voted against capping insulin prices at $35 a month for seniors. They voted against cracking down on Big Oil’s price gouging at the pump. They’re attempting to reverse the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau’s new plan to cap credit card junk fees. I could write a whole email about each of those different shameful actions. But here’s what I’ll focus on today: Congressional Republicans are also trying to repeal the IRS’s new free tax filing program — in other words, they’re trying to force Americans to fork over money to big tax prep companies. We can’t let them succeed. [**Add your name to say you support the IRS’s Direct File program and oppose Republicans’ attempts to repeal it. And let’s fight them side by side.**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/signup/ew-em-DirectFile/?source=EMZ20Z_TAX_E_20240621_V1S1&t=8&akid=2231%2E4032634%2E-NSXZV) | [**ADD YOUR NAME**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/signup/ew-em-DirectFile/?source=EMZ20Z_TAX_E_20240621_V1S1&t=9&akid=2231%2E4032634%2E-NSXZV)
---
Now you might remember that we’ve been fighting tooth and nail for free tax filing. I’ve introduced legislation, we’ve raised our voices, we’ve pushed back against the swarms of lobbyists from big tax firms trying to stop us — and as part of the Inflation Reduction Act, we secured funding to make it happen.
This year, the IRS launched the Direct File pilot program for 12 states — including Massachusetts! And it was a big success:
* Over 140,000 taxpayers used the tool
* They saved more than $90 million in refunds and an estimated $5.6 million in tax preparation fees on their federal returns alone
* A survey of 11,000 users found that 90% ranked their experience with Direct File as “Excellent” or “Above Average”
* And 90% of survey respondents who used customer service similarly found the experience “Excellent” or “Above Average”

Based on these great results, I urged the IRS to expand the program and make it permanent.
That’s exactly what they did. Last month, we got the terrific news that millions more Americans will get the option to file directly with the IRS — rather than waste an average of 9 hours and $150 with shady tax prep giants like TurboTax and H&R Block.
Sounds great, right? Who could object? Apparently, Republican U.S. House members. After all, the GOP wants to help big corporations — like Big Pharma, Big Oil, the credit card industry, and tax prep giants like Intuit TurboTax and H&R Block — look after their bottom lines. So they’re trying to repeal this good thing that the government is doing for working people.
While Republican politicians continue catering to corporate interests and trying to keep costs high for working people, I’ll continue fighting to tackle corporate greed and bring down costs. Including for the tax filing process.
**Tax filing should be fast and free, no matter how mad it makes the big tax prep giants.** But House Republicans are trying to end the Direct File program before it has a chance to get fully off the ground. We can’t let them. We’ve got to fight back.
[**If you agree, add your name here, and we’ll fight together to stop the GOP’s attacks on the Direct File program.**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/signup/ew-em-DirectFile/?source=EMZ20Z_TAX_E_20240621_V1S1&t=10&akid=2231%2E4032634%2E-NSXZV)
Thanks for being a part of this,
Elizabeth
